summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY, with hands-on experience in low-level C/C++ systems programming across bare-metal microcontrollers, FreeRTOS-based real-time systems, and Linux-based embedded platforms. Built STM32 Cortex-M4 firmware with direct register-level peripheral control, validated through iterative hardware testing. Comfortable diagnosing and resolving integration failures end-to-end in real-time embedded systems.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate hand motion into HID commands via Python; debugged and resolved sensor jitter through calibration.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design and PCB fabrication.
Designed and fabricated custom PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Developed a custom image-stitching pipeline using bit manipulation and averaging, achieving a PSNR (a standard video/image quality metric) of 65 versus a homography baseline.
Designed a custom wavelet bank to suppress low-frequency noise, improving PSNR to 86 through optimized stitching and concurrency.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination across concurrent sensing and control tasks.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART command handling and user override.
Used YOLOv8 on Jetson (Linux-based) for detection, relaying commands to STM32 over UART with VL53L0X ToF sensing.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Diagnosed and resolved 11 integration failures through iterative testing, achieving 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s latency.
Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++, driving five servos with range-gated contact detection.
Integrated TensorRT-optimized YOLO for visual servoing, a 5.2× speedup (56.7→10.9 ms) over eager PyTorch.
